data.hypothesis: A matching 256-thread CTA and 256-source tile may reduce tile-loop and synchronization overhead while letting each staged source serve 256 target threads. This uses more shared memory per CTA than the measured 128/128 configuration, so occupancy or resource costs may offset that reuse; official timing must decide.
data.notes: This is a new 256/256 configuration, not a speedup claim. Prior search measurements provide comparison context: 128/128 was valid at 0.0008998 s (1ee0d3b3e82e43a5), while 256/128 and 128/256 were slower (87e259578e29474c; a47fd303c1344204). The controller must run the full correctness suite and official timing for this candidate.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 256 and configure 4096 bytes for a 256-entry, 16-byte shared source tile.
Cooperatively stage bounded source chunks and synchronize before consumption and before replacing each chunk; keep all threads participating, including inactive target-tail threads.

Keep one target and force accumulator per thread, exclude self-interactions by global index, guard partial source tiles and target tails, and preserve particle mass and the original integration expressions.
